name: South Africa
dated: Rates and Monetary Amounts and Amendment of Revenue Laws Acts 21 of 2018, 19 of 2023, 45 of 2024 and 3 of 2026 (official PDFs from sars.gov.za, Government Gazette prints); SARS rate pages for the dividends tax
sources: Sources: SARS web pages saved locally (`cmp20/world/B02-g20/za/law/sars_intdiv.html`); the acts held by Global law are not reached (GL) in this pass. Amending acts fetched from sars.gov.za (redirects to wp-content/uploads/Legal/AmendActs/*.pdf), saved in `cmp20/global/R4/fetch/za8/` with SHA256SUMS and layout text.

vat.name: Value Added Tax
vat.statute: Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 s. 7 (1) as amended by the Rates and Monetary Amounts and Amendment of Revenue Laws Act 21 of 2018 s. 9 (15 % from 1 April 2018); the 2025 budget increase did not take effect (Act 3 of 2026 s. 13, deemed from 1 May 2025)
vat.doc: Act 21 of 2018 s. 9 (1) (a): section 7 (1) of the VAT Act is amended so that the tax is "calculated at the rate of [14] 15 per cent on the value of the supply concerned or the importation". Act 3 of 2026 s. 13 (1): "Despite (a) section 7(4) of the Value-Added Tax Act, 1991; and (b) the announcement by the Minister of Finance on 12 March 2025 in the national annual budget ... the alteration of the VAT rate specified in section 7 of that Act, 1991, does not come into effect"; (2) deemed in effect from 1 May 2025. So 15 % applied throughout 2025.
notes: VAT Act s. 11 zero-rating (basic foodstuffs, Schedule 2 Part B) and s. 12 exemptions (financial services, residential rent, passenger transport, education) are not applied: the consolidated VAT Act was not read

excise.name: Specific excise duties (Schedule 1 Part 2A)
excise.statute: Customs and Excise Act 1964 Schedule No. 1 Part 2A: to 11 March 2025 as amended by the Rates and Monetary Amounts and Amendment of Revenue Laws Act 45 of 2024 s. 1 and Part I of the Schedule (deemed from 21 February 2024); from 12 March 2025 as amended by Act 3 of 2026 s. 4 and Schedule II (deemed from 12 March 2025)
excise.doc: 2024/2025 rates: SA Act 45 of 2024 s. 1 (2) ('deemed to have come into operation on 21 February 2024') and Part I: '104.10.20 2203.00.90 Other R135.89/li aa', '104.15.03 2204.21.41 ... R5.57/li', '104.23.05 2208.30.10 ... R274.39/li aa', '104.30.07 2402.20.90 Other R10.89/10 cigarettes'; 2025/2026 rates: SA Act 3 of 2026 s. 4 (2) (12 March 2025) and Sch. II: R145.07/li aa, R5.95/li, R292.91/li aa, R11.40/10 (R4/fetch/za8/act-45-of-2024.txt, act-3-of-2026.txt). Each rate applies on its window; an undated line bears each on its share of the year (70/365 and 295/365).

cit.name: Corporate income tax
cit.statute: Income Tax Act 1962 s. 5 (2); Rates and Monetary Amounts and Amendment of Revenue Laws Act 3 of 2026 Schedule I para 3 (a) (27 %, years of assessment ending on or after 1 April 2025); Act 19 of 2023 Schedule para 3 (a) (27 %, years ending on or after 1 April 2023)
cit.doc: Act 3 of 2026, Schedule I para 3: "The rate of tax referred to in section 2(1) to be levied in respect of the taxable income of a company (other than a public benefit organization, recreational club or small business funding entity referred to in paragraph 4 or a small business corporation referred to in paragraph 5), in respect of any year of assessment ending on or after 1 April 2025 is, subject to the provisions of paragraph 12, as follows: (a) 27 per cent of the taxable income of any company". Act 19 of 2023 para 3 (a) prints the same 27 % for years ending on or after 1 April 2023.
notes: small business corporations (para 5, 0-27 % bands), gold mining formula and long-term insurers' funds (para 3 (b)-(d)) not modelled; assessed losses are carried forward under s. 20 (80 % limit above R1 million from 2023, not modelled)

wht.name: Dividends tax
wht.statute: Income Tax Act 1962 s. 64E (20 %), per the SARS page (official secondary); twelfth pass: Income Tax Act 1962 s. 50A-50H (withholding tax on interest 15 %, final; SARS page fetched 2026-11-21, R4/fetch/za12, official secondary); Income Tax Act 1962 s. 49A-49H (withholding tax on royalties 15 %, final; SARS page fetched 2026-11-21, R4/fetch/za12, official secondary)
wht.doc: SARS dividends-tax page (budget update of 25 February 2026: no change; facts, paraphrased): 20 % dividends tax, withheld by the company paying the dividend. Withholding tax on interest and royalties (15 %) not read. Twelfth pass (kernel 2.3.0 grade-C withholding): interest 15 %: Income Tax Act 1962 s. 50A-50H (withholding tax on interest 15 %, final; SARS page fetched 2026-11-21, R4/fetch/za12, official secondary); royalty 15 %: Income Tax Act 1962 s. 49A-49H (withholding tax on royalties 15 %, final; SARS page fetched 2026-11-21, R4/fetch/za12, official secondary)

rules.statute: Income Tax Act 1962 s. 50A-50H (withholding tax on interest 15 %, final; SARS page fetched 2026-11-21, R4/fetch/za12, official secondary)
Income Tax Act 1962 s. 49A-49H (withholding tax on royalties 15 %, final; SARS page fetched 2026-11-21, R4/fetch/za12, official secondary)

notes: South Africa: dividends tax, withholding tax on interest and on royalties (SARS pages, official secondary); services left C (taxed by assessment)
unsupported: services paid to a non-resident: SARS administers no withholding tax on service fees (its list of taxes, `R4/fetch/za12/types-of-tax.html`, has dividends tax and withholding taxes on interest and royalties only); the non-resident is taxed by assessment on South African-source service income, which the model does not compute: left grade C (no cited 0)
